clue.text: Burst of cheering enveloping Newfoundland flier

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping round, so the shuffled letters close around the abbreviation
a burst breaks something apart, so the letters of cheering are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: NF is the standard abbreviation for the Canadian province of Newfoundland

explanation.surface: A roar of applause surrounds an aviator arriving from Newfoundland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burst of' scrambles the cheering into GREEICH, which 'enveloping' wraps round the province's letters. 'Flier' suggests an aviator, but here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A finch is a small songbird, and any bird can be called a flier in crosswords.

clue.text: An issue of violence or sentiment?

definitions.meaning: a violent outpouring, as of water or blood from a wound
effusive, overdone emotional talk

explanation.surface: A question asking whether something stems from brutality or from feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden violent flood of liquid and a stream of mawkish praise share the same word.

clue.text: A performance of capital detachment?

definitions.meaning: the carrying out of a piece of music or a plan
separating the head (the capital, from Latin caput) from the body: a beheading

explanation.surface: A show staged in the capital city by some aloof performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city, but it means the head, so 'capital detachment' is beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician's rendering and an act of putting someone to death share this noun.

clue.text: Fibre man made from tawny long-johns

indicators.note: from tells us to take the answer out of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Someone's long underwear in a brownish colour turns out to be synthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across tawNY LONg-johns, signalled by 'from'.
explanation.definitionFit: This synthetic polymer was the first wholly artificial textile fibre, made in a laboratory.

clue.text: An ailing body of no legal standing

definitions.meaning: a sick person, one who is unwell for a long time
void, having no force in law

explanation.surface: A sick person who also lacks any legal rights.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: IN-va-lid for the sick person, in-VAL-id for the void document.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-term patient and a void contract share a spelling but differ in stress.

clue.text: A country seat that might intoxicate one in France

definitions.meaning: a large house on a rural estate

definitions.text: that might intoxicate one in France
definitions.meaning: a French wine estate's name, as on a bottle label of claret, can make a drinker tipsy

explanation.surface: A French manor house whose cellar could get a visitor drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A French castle or manor, and the Bordeaux wines named after such estates.

clue.text: Border on an objection

parts.note: the indefinite article gives the single letter A
a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Advice about how to make a protest that nearly crosses the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch along an edge, as adjoining plots of land do.

clue.text: A constructive masonic order?

parts.note: read not as a Freemasons' lodge but as a command shouted to stonemasons telling them to construct

explanation.surface: A lodge of Freemasons that is helpful rather than critical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masonic order' suggests the Freemasons, but it is an instruction given to bricklayers and stonemasons.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperative telling workmen to erect a wall or house is the command a mason obeys.

clue.text: Difficult period for the courts to assemble

definitions.meaning: a hard, stressful spell
the hour when judges sit to hear cases, a time for putting people on trial

explanation.surface: A hard spell when the law courts gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A testing phase of life, and literally the hour at which courts begin hearing cases.

clue.text: Party takes weapons but apparently not for the front

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or game
arms are weapons

explanation.surface: A political group arms itself, though not to fight at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the name: pistols worn at the hip, by one's side rather than carried forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols or swords carried at the hip, worn by one's flank rather than ahead.

clue.text: A dandy enlargement

definitions.meaning: a fashionably dressed man, a toff
a bulge or ..., also a rising of the sea

explanation.surface: A fop who is also a swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a fashionable gentleman, and a puffed-up bulge or heave of the sea.

clue.text: Six bringing skill to working practicality

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
ability is skill or competence

explanation.surface: A team of six brings know-how to a practical working arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasibility: the capacity of a plan to operate successfully.

clue.text: A very cold body may often swing from left to right

definitions.text: A very cold body may often
definitions.meaning: a freezing person's skin takes on a bluish tinge
change political allegiance to the Conservatives, whose colour in Britain is blue

explanation.surface: A frozen figure swaying from side to side.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Conservative party's colour is blue, so a left-winger moving right adopts that colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivering skin taking on a bluish hue, and a voter changing to the Tory side.

clue.text: One way to see the point of Donne translation

definitions.text: One way to see the point

indicators.note: translation renders words in another form, so the poet's name is turned into new letters

explanation.surface: A suggested reading of the poet John Donne that helps one grasp his meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation' rearranges DONNE. 'See the point' sounds like understanding, but it means looking at a sharp tip head-first.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing something with its tip towards you, so the pointed end is in view.

clue.text: Prepare some firewood for the Chinese on board?

definitions.meaning: cut kindling into pieces with an axe
the eating utensils used in China, at the table, board being an old word for a dining table

explanation.surface: Getting kindling ready for Chinese people aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' looks like aboard a ship, but 'board' is a table, as in 'bed and board'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacking up kindling, and the pair of slender sticks used for eating in China.

clue.text: Having entertained guests all round I heaved up

indicators.note: all round says the first word goes right round the second

parts.note: hosted means having entertained guests

explanation.surface: After throwing a party for everyone, the host lifted something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All round' puts I inside HOSTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised by rope or tackle, lifted aloft as a flag is.

clue.text: Swinging movement getting nowhere among bureaucrats!

definitions.meaning: a back-and-forth motion, like a pendulum's
paperwork shuttling between officials without progress

explanation.surface: Officials who swing back and forth and achieve nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Motion back and forth, also the futile passing of files between officials.

clue.text: Utter chaos as nothing goes correctly for old Rhine city

indicators.note: put correctly means set right, so jumbled letters are arranged into proper order

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Total confusion in a Dutch city where nothing goes right.
explanation.walkthrough: From UTTER CHAOS the letters of AS and O (nothing) 'go', and what is left is put 'correctly' in order. The Oude Rijn, the old course of the Rhine, flows through this Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch cathedral city standing on the Oude Rijn, the Rhine's ancient channel.

clue.text: Old cavalry officer is training first instrumentalist

parts.note: a cornet was formerly the lowest commissioned officer in a British cavalry troop

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word training

explanation.surface: A retired cavalry officer is now in training before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' takes T, the start of 'training'. 'Old cavalry officer' looks like the definition, but it supplies CORNET.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the cornet, a small brass horn, is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Not an ideal landing, getting tossed and turned

definitions.meaning: a belly-flop landing in which an aircraft drops flat onto the ground
a thin batter cake flipped in the pan

explanation.surface: A bumpy touchdown that leaves passengers thrown about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossed and turned' sounds like a sleepless night, but it is what is done to the batter in the frying pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat crash-landing of a plane, and the flat batter cake flipped in the air.

clue.text: A crude cipher redrawn in Andean country

indicators.note: redrawn means sketched again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cipher is a zero, written O

explanation.surface: A rough coded map is drawn up again in a South American nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redrawn' rearranges A, CRUDE and O. 'Cipher' looks like a code, but it is the old sense: zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic in South America straddling the Andes mountain chain and the equator.

clue.text: Peculiar sort in odd setting for the platform

indicators.note: in shows the jumbled letters set inside the other word

parts.note: rum is old slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: peculiar means strange or out of the ordinary, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A strange type in an unusual setting stands at the speaker's stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' rearranges SORT into OSTR, which goes 'in' RUM (odd), RUM forming its setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stand from which a speaker addresses an audience or a conductor directs.

clue.text: Reeling peer allowed in, tanked up

indicators.note: in shows the word for allowed placed inside the jumbled letters
reeling means staggering about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A staggering nobleman, admitted to the party, is plainly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reeling' turns PEER into REPE, and LET goes 'in'. 'Tanked up' hints at drunkenness, but here it just means full.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled to capacity, stuffed full, as a well-fed diner or loaded tank is.

clue.text: It's essential an old television should be backing a first appearance

definitions.text: It's essential an old television should be

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a debut is a first appearance on stage or in sport

explanation.surface: A vintage TV must support a newcomer's first show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns DEBUT round. Old televisions worked by cathode-ray tubes, so one had to be fitted with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Old sets relied on valves and a cathode-ray tube, so they had to be fitted with tubes.

clue.text: A noble joint

definitions.meaning: a member of the lowest rank of the peerage
a large cut of beef, both loins joined at the backbone

explanation.surface: A two-word note pairing an aristocrat with a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'baron of beef' is a large roasting joint, the double sirloin.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the lowest rank, and a huge cut of beef with both sirloins.

clue.text: Put United Nations first? On the contrary

definitions.text: Put United Nations first? On the contrary

indicators.note: first says the organisation's letters come before the word for put

parts.note: placed means put or set down

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the UN should be given priority, and the answer is no.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks a policy question, but the whole clue builds the word and defines it: 'On the contrary' turns 'put first' into its opposite, not finishing in the top places of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or runner not finishing among the leading positions in a race.

clue.text: Seething Nazi circle where the Allies broke in

indicators.note: seething means boiling with agitation, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: An angry ring of Nazi troops at the site of a wartime invasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seething' rearranges NAZI. In January 1944 the Allies landed at this Italian port to break into German-held Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian coastal town where Allied forces made an amphibious landing in 1944.

clue.text: Apprehension of force flying up around East

indicators.note: around shows the reversed word placed round the compass point
in a down clue flying up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force, is a force

explanation.surface: The air force soaring up over the East causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying up' turns RAF into FAR, which goes 'around' E. The grid's PEAR is a misprint: the definition and wordplay both give FEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread or anxiety about what may happen is a synonym, as in feeling uneasy dread.

clue.text: A farm vehicle on hill range carries the gunpowder

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the casing that holds the powder charge for a gun

parts.note: a cart is a farm vehicle
a ridge is a long range of hills

explanation.surface: A farm wagon on a ridge of hills is loaded with explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the thing does rather than naming it: the case holding a firearm's charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The case that holds a bullet's propellant charge for loading into a firearm.

clue.text: Substituting zebra's heart I transformed an African runner

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the resulting letters are rearranged
substituting tells us to swap one letter of the animal's name for another

parts.note: the striped animal's name is written out in full

explanation.surface: Swapping a zebra for something else, I turned into a sprinter from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'heart' of ZEBRA is its middle letter B; 'Substituting' puts I in its place, giving ZEIRA, which is 'transformed'. 'Runner' is the crossword's river, here the Congo's former name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo river was once called by this name, and in crosswords any river is a runner.

clue.text: Go down in the kitchen

definitions.meaning: to fall or descend below the surface
the basin with taps where dishes are washed

explanation.surface: A note about a fall in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop below water, and the basin under the kitchen taps.

clue.text: The roving pirate who gives away his last products?

definitions.meaning: a buccaneer who roams the seas plundering

definitions.text: who gives away his last products
definitions.meaning: a shoemaker, whose last is the foot-shaped block, handing out boots for nothing

explanation.surface: A wandering buccaneer turns out to be a generous cobbler.
explanation.walkthrough: A cobbler's 'last' is the foot-shaped mould on which boots are made, so 'last products' are boots, handed out free.
explanation.definitionFit: A plundering adventurer, and literally someone handing out free footwear.
